text:
R431 — phase/head-lease decode expert-cache budget
Date: 2026-10-13
Scope: read-only source audit; no runtime, log, benchmark, GPU, process, environment, build, test, AST, or cleanup inspection.
Frozen source: /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-layer-major-phase4k-20261013
HEAD: db088ff24e67e6a4566566dfc4762c63c55bf343

Finding
The 144 -> 912 count is an explicitly bounded experiment layout, not a measurement of free VRAM and not a source claim that 912 slots physically fit. The phase arm reserves a capped virtual address layout, starts with 144 mapped slots (3 per each of 48 layers), and conditionally maps another 768 (16 per layer) only after prefill. The actual physical fit remains a runtime admission question. No hit-rate, throughput, or optimal-cache claim follows from this source audit.

Why those counts
In src/program/generate.cpp, the phase-mode admission requires the constrained serve setup: one GPU, no MTP/batch/pipeline, no prefill borrowing, fixed prefill chunk, PCIe fraction zero, adaptive swaps zero, INT8 KV, max context 262144, resident 32768, no KV growth, expert-cache 128 plus per-layer flag, immutable full profile and the expected 48-layer/512-expert geometry. The arm requires ordinary requested cache size 144 and verifies 144 selected profile slots. It then opens the phase owner with 512 experts/layer, 16 extra ranks/layer, and an 8-GiB virtual-reservation ceiling. The 16 is a constexpr experimental budget, not a measured optimum.

The profile supplies top-3 experts per layer as the baseline (3*48=144). The owner reserves room for an additional 16*48=768, giving capacity 912. It fills/publishes baseline after prefill, then tries all extras as a single admission. If admitted, decode has all 19 selected experts/layer resident. If rejected, the owner does not dynamically choose a smaller extra count: the phase operation fails. The profile and adapt-swaps=0 make this a static set; routed experts outside the selected top-19 use the existing CPU/source path. There is no replacement policy in this phase owner.

The byte ratio is useful only as a logical payload estimate: each expert blob is equal-sized per layer; 3/512 of the complete expert payload is baseline and 16/512 is the extra tranche. On the cited 50.292-GB logical full expert payload, that is about 0.295 GB baseline, 1.572 GB extra, 1.867 GB total, before map/granularity/alignment and runtime allocation overhead. This is not the physical allocation total. The 8 GiB cap limits reserved virtual address space; it does not preallocate or certify physical backing.

Meaning of --expert-cache128 --expert-cache-per-layer
These are required phase-arm admission tokens, not an instruction to give every layer 128 slots, and not the active phase cache count. In the ordinary per-layer policy, slots are distributed as quotient/remainder across layers: for 128 over 48, first 47 layers receive 2 and the last receives 34. In the phase path ordinary open is superseded by the phase owner and its fixed profile map (3 base plus up to 16 extras per layer). Treating 128 as 128-per-layer would be wrong.

Decode-only increase and lifecycle
The existing lease sequence creates a prefill opportunity by retiring readers and releasing the native head, then unmapping all expert cache backing for prefill while retaining the phase virtual reservation. Prefill allocates its bounded workspace. After successful prefill, its implementation and lazy allocations are destroyed; the cache maps and fills the baseline, reloads the native head, and maps/fills extras. Thus extra physical cache can be decode-only. On the next fresh generation extras are invalidated/unmapped back to 144; the next prefill lease detaches baseline too. This cycle makes no claim that a stock READY-time free reading predicts post-prefill free space.

Extra mapping is all-or-nothing. It checks fresh VMM capability, free bytes, maximum allocation size and granularity, required extent size, and a separate 512-MiB free-space margin; the virtual extent is also bounded by the 8-GiB reservation. A failed/uncertain map is fail-stop. It does not shrink to the number of slots that happen to fit. These are source guardrails, not evidence that a target device passes them.

What occupies or survives the prefill lease
- Expert cache: phase invalidation/unmap removes physical backing for both baseline and extra slots during prefill; the reserved VA remains. Afterward baseline and optional extra mappings are distinct tranches.
- Native head: NativeHead::release_for_prefill frees the device weight and scratch allocations while preserving a CPU source snapshot. reload_after_prefill recreates the GPU allocations. Generate prints exact head weight/scratch and free-before/after values during a run, but no run values were read here.
- QSA/KV state: session state is persistent across the lease. For max context 262144 and page size 4, each QSA layer's logical table has 65,536 pages/cells and its identity-layout INT8 host KV backing covers the full context. With 32,768 resident cells the device pool uses 8,192 pages; it is a sliding/streamed resident window, not a 32K-context state. Page table, indexer state, and RoPE table are also sized from max context (the shared RoPE table is allocated once). KV streaming therefore saves VRAM, but reserves host memory and retains the full-context metadata/state.
- Verifier: init allocates a persistent device arena and mapped host staging. In this task raw --spec 4 is the verifier maximum buffer size, while the actual non-MTP decode window is one token. The verifier's phase graph retirement drops graphs/graph segments and per-window graph structures; it does not free the arena, mapped staging, streams/events, or profile state. Those allocations can still consume device/mapped memory during prompt prefill. Do not mistake graph retirement for verifier destruction.
- Prefill: phase_capacity_estimate bounds workspace, token and identity buffers, conditional chooser/lazy-GEMM allocations, and the configured runtime reserve. GDN/QSA/MoE buffers are subregions of the shared workspace extent, so its estimate counts their maximum, not the sum. The admission compares this requested bound to a fresh free query after head/cache release and rejects if it is too large; it prints physical_fit_proof=0 because backend/JIT/provider/fragmentation uncertainty remains. The --vram-reserve-mib 700 is a requested prefill runtime reserve, separate from the phase owner's 512-MiB extra-map margin.
- Graph capture/runtime: decode graphs are captured with the post-prefill owners live. Their graph-private allocations and backend/runtime overhead are not converted into a static byte guarantee by the 8-GiB VA cap or 512-MiB guard.

Minimum actual allocation evidence Main should collect
For one successful, representative run on the target device, capture the owner's requested and actual mapped/retained physical byte counts and slot counts at four boundaries: initial baseline; immediately after prefill/head release and before workspace reinit; after prefill workspace destruction and baseline remap/head reload; after extra-map and decode graph capture. At each boundary record device total/free from the same backend, per-allocation requested/actual bytes and owner for expert base/extra extents, native head weight/scratch, persistent QSA/KV device pools and verifier arena, plus workspace and any graph/backend allocations that differ across the boundary. Also record full-context pinned KV bytes and process-level host memory separately from device memory. Include success/failure of the 512-MiB guard, extent granularities and max-allocation query. Preserve exact raw --spec=4 and actual NT=1 separately. This is the minimal evidence needed to answer “enough?”; a single total-free number cannot explain ownership or fragmentation.

Safe follow-ups (not performance claims)
1. Keep the current fixed 16-extra-per-layer tranche as an explicit experiment ceiling. If broader capacity is needed, make extra count an operator-selected bounded parameter and compute the per-layer extent from the requested count; retain all-or-nothing admission, fresh-free query, runtime margin, max-allocation/granularity checks, and fail-stop behavior. Validate actual allocations before changing defaults.
2. Add a compact per-owner phase memory ledger at the existing lifecycle boundaries, reporting requested versus backend-confirmed bytes, without inferring post-prefill space from startup/READY values. This is safer than a hardware-total-only cache heuristic and makes later policy changes reviewable.

Source locations reviewed
src/program/generate.cpp: phase guards and owner open (~4186-4250); phase lifecycle callbacks (~8035-8310), fresh-free/requested peak admission and cache transition.
src/core/layer.cpp: kv_plan, qsa_state_bytes/init (~650-850); context-size metadata, resident KV slots, host copy, shared RoPE.
src/core/native_head.cpp: release/reload ownership (~131-150).
src/core/verify.cpp: Verifier::init staging and device arena (~221-380); graph retirement/destruction (~source Verifier methods).
PhaseCacheOwner implementation: phase reserve/map/unmap/fresh budget checks and fixed base/extra extent layout.

Status and limits
This report is an explanation of frozen source behavior only. It does not establish that any concrete GPU has enough physical memory, that 912 slots map successfully, or that the new phase improves decode performance. Main's GPU qualification is in progress; do not infer results from this report.
scope: Source-only research; no new runtime qualification
